brief: DevOps: build a GitHub Actions CI workflow YAML for a small Python stdlib project plus a built-ins-only PowerShell checker that validates the workflow structure, with a -SelfTest mode; then an evidence-collector QA task that independently verifies it. No downloads, no installs, nothing registered or pushed; deliverables stay in the mission output folder.
summary: DevOps Automator v2 built a GitHub Actions CI workflow, a built-ins-only PowerShell checker with a 28-case self-test and a sample project; Evidence Collector re-verified it (PASS) and listed 4 non-blocking checker gaps.

tasks.task: Write ci.yml, a GitHub Actions CI workflow for a small Python stdlib project, plus Test-Workflow.ps1, a built-ins-only PowerShell checker for it, plus a tiny sample project (package + unittest tests) so the workflow test command can be run locally
acceptance: ci.yml triggers on push and pull_request, has a job with runs-on, a strategy.matrix python-version list of 3 or more versions, uses actions/checkout and actions/setup-python pinned to a version tag, and has a step running python -m unittest
Test-Workflow.ps1 -Path ci.yml exits 0 on the delivered workflow and prints one PASS or FAIL line per check

Test-Workflow.ps1 -SelfTest feeds at least 5 broken workflows (for example missing on, missing jobs, tab indentation, job without runs-on, unpinned action) and exits 0 only if every broken one is rejected
The sample project tests pass locally with the same unittest command the workflow runs, with the output saved under evidence/
Only PowerShell built-ins and the installed Python are used; nothing is downloaded, installed, registered or pushed

tasks.task: Write Rotate-Backups.ps1 (Windows PowerShell 5.1 compatible) plus Test-Rotate.ps1 self-test and README.md
